content: Magnesium iodide refers to the chemical compounds with the formulas MgI₂ and its various hydrates, represented as MgI₂(H₂O)x. These compounds are typical ionic halides, characterized by their high solubility in water. While magnesium iodide has limited commercial applications, it is utilized in the preparation of compounds for organic synthesis. Magnesium iodide can be synthesized through the reaction of magnesium oxide, magnesium hydroxide, or magnesium carbonate with hydroiodic acid. This compound remains stable under high temperatures in a hydrogen atmosphere. However, when exposed to air at normal temperatures, it undergoes decomposition, releasing elemental iodine, which causes the compound to turn brown.
